  &= (y+3)(3-(y+3))^{2} \\
  &= (y+3)\,(-y)^{2}=y^2(y+3)
  =y^3+3y^2 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Using (1) to replace \(y^3\),

\[
y^3+3y^2 = (6y-6)+3y^2 = 3y^2+6y-6
          =3\bigl(y^2+2y-2\bigr). \tag{2}
\]

Now set \(z=y^2+2y-2\).  From \(y^3-6y+6=0\) we obtain a cubic
for the quantity \(u=y+1\):
\[
(y+1)^3-3(y+1)^2-3(y+1)+11=0 .
\]
Writing \(u=y+1\) gives  

\[
u^3-3u^2-3u+11=0 .
\]

The required value (2) can be expressed in terms of \(u\) as  

\[
x(3-x)^2 = 3\bigl(u^2-3\bigr).\tag{3}
\]

From the cubic for \(u\),

\[
u^3-3u^2-3u+11=0\Longrightarrow (u-3)^3+108=0,
\]
hence  

\[
u-3 =\sqrt[3]{-108} = -3\sqrt[3]{4}.
\]

Thus  

\[
u = 3-3\sqrt[3]{4}.
\]

Substituting this \(u\) into (3),

\[
\begin{aligned}
x(3-x)^2 
   &= 3\bigl[(3-3\sqrt[3]{4})^{2}-3\bigr] \\
   &= 3\Bigl[9-18\sqrt[3]{4}+9\sqrt[3]{16}-3\Bigr] \\
   &= 6-3\sqrt[3]{4}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Since the original cubic has only one real root, the real value of
\(x(3-x)^2\) is

\[
\boxed{6-3\sqrt[3]{4}}.
\]

(If one also admits the two complex roots of the original cubic,
the other two values are \(6-3\sqrt[3]{4}\,\omega\) and
\(6-3\sqrt[3]{4}\,\omega^{2}\), where 
\(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\) is a primitive cube root of unity.)<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
